svg.title: The RAMC Chain of Evacuation on the Western Front (1914–1918)
svg.desc: Left-to-right cross-sectional terrain and medical logistics diagram of the RAMC Chain of Evacuation on the Western Front: 1. Stretcher Bearers (12%, 58%), 2. Regimental Aid Post (30%, 52%), 3. Field Ambulance ADS and MDS (49%, 48%), 4. Casualty Clearing Station (70%, 44%), and 5. Coastal Base Hospital and Hospital Ships (89%, 40%).
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · ROYAL ARMY MEDICAL CORPS (RAMC) & FANY LOGISTICS
The RAMC Chain of Evacuation on the Western Front (1914–1918)
TRANSPORT EVOLUTION ACROSS THE EVACUATION PIPELINE (WHY SPEED SAVED LIVES AGAINST GAS GANGRENE)
mud slowed carry to hours; high
• Public Times appeal bought 512 motor vans;
6-horse wagons still vital in deep mud.
night convoys under air raids, repaired
engines & freed male orderlies for front.
KEY EXAM STAT · WHY THE CCS BECAME THE DECISIVE SURGICAL STAGE
Waiting for Base Hospitals let gas gangrene kill men in 24 hrs; moving surgery forward to
the CCS + Thomas Splints (Dec 1915) cut compound femur mortality from 80% to under 20%!
RAMC THREE-CATEGORY TRIAGE SYSTEM AT ADS / CCS
1. Walking Wounded: Patch & return to unit · 2. Urgent Surgery: Immediate theatre /
transfusion at CCS · 3. Moribund (Beyond Saving): Morphine & quiet comfort care.
